The friction is visible and rising: Trump called the package 'a very good negotiating chip' after the Beijing summit (14-16 May 2026), said he is 'not looking to have somebody go independent', raised the Six Assurances question, hosted Xi on 23-25 Sep 2026 (Beijing says Xi asked the US to oppose independence; the White House fact sheet is silent on Taiwan), and Lutnick wants 40% of the chip chain moved to the US while the 15% tariff stays negotiable. Washington's own line is 'unchanged' (Rubio). Grade is our reading of structure (confidence C): sources describe the relationship as unofficial, strategic ambiguity and, since May, as transactional. Bond - affinity: democratic kinship, Congress and the Taiwanese diaspora; no grievance.
